final_title: Subarray-Level Delay Lines from W1 Photonic-Crystal Waveguides for Beam-Squint Reduction: A Computational Study
final_central_claim: In a 2-D lossless FDTD/MPB model, a plain W1 photonic-crystal waveguide gives delay increments of 3.93 a/c per period (0.981 carrier cycle, 0.04 % band-fit accuracy) over a validated 14.8 % fractional bandwidth; with one channel and one constant phase trim per four-element lambda0/2 subarray at 30 deg (required 1.000 cycle, 1.9 % mismatch) the maximum pointing error over the band is 0.19 deg against 2.69 deg for fixed phase, strongest sidelobe -12.4 dB, replica lobes <= -16.6 dB. This supports the feasibility of subarray-level PhC delay lines for beam-squint reduction; it does not demonstrate a device.

wording_decisions.dispersion_engineered: dropped (plain W1 selected; engineering tried and rejected in Phase 3)
wording_decisions.broadband: qualified as 14.8 % validated, domain-limited fractional bandwidth
wording_decisions.true_time_delay: delay slope only; trimmed family = TTD slope plus one constant phase trim per channel, never ideal TTD
wording_decisions.coincidence: Msub = 4 match is n_g f0 about 0.98 at 30 deg, not a design principle

selected_architecture: Msub = 4 subarray-level delay: 4 PhC channels (N = 8-11), 16 lambda0/2 elements, one constant phase trim per channel re-chosen for the required step, theta0 = 30 deg
restrictions: post-data Phase 4 convergence correction (common minimum run time)
only one steering angle (30 deg) studied for the architectural match
Msub = 8 with two-period spacing not simulated
no conventional-delay-line comparison beyond MPB-only reference
no literature survey; no novelty claim
historical_corrections: Phase 0.5 geometry sign bug and branch-tracking bug (rerun)
Phase 2 validated-band boundary chosen post hoc
Phase 3 hole-shift sign bug fixed, D1/D2 rerun
Phase 6 first Monte Carlo sign convention discarded and rerun
arxiv_readiness: B: nearly ready; manuscript gap = references and literature positioning; scientific gap = no conventional-line comparison beyond MPB-only (restricts claim to feasibility); no numerical validation gap blocking; no further simulation recommended
